reference.title: Perihilar (Ch. 25) vs Distal (Ch. 26) extrahepatic bile duct landmarks
reference.intro: The insertion of the cystic duct separates perihilar bile ducts (proximal: right/left hepatic ducts, confluence, common hepatic duct) from the distal extrahepatic bile duct (common bile duct down to the ampulla).
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Perihilar bile ducts (AJCC 8th Chapter 25)
points: Staged by anatomic extent: pT1 confined to duct wall, pT2a periductal adipose tissue, pT2b adjacent hepatic parenchyma, pT3 unilateral portal vein/hepatic artery, pT4 main/bilateral vessels or bilateral 2nd-order biliary radicals.

groups.heading: Distal extrahepatic bile duct (AJCC 8th Chapter 26)
points: Staged strictly by measured depth of invasion from the basement membrane of adjacent normal epithelium (or deepest invasive point if ulcerated): pT1 < 5 mm, pT2 5–12 mm, pT3 > 12 mm; pT4 involves coeliac axis, SMA, or common hepatic artery.

reference.title: Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma histology & mimics
reference.intro: Most extrahepatic bile duct carcinomas are pancreatobiliary-type adenocarcinomas eliciting dense desmoplasia and extensive perineural invasion. Distinguish well-differentiated invasive glands from reactive peribiliary glands.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Pancreatobiliary-type adenocarcinoma
points: Widely spaced, angulated irregular glands and single cells in a desmoplastic stroma; nuclear size variation >= 4:1, loss of polarity, intraluminal necrotic debris, and frequent perineural invasion.
Benign peribiliary glands retain lobular architecture with uniform basal nuclei and lack desmoplasia.

images.caption: Cholangiocarcinoma: infiltrating irregular malignant glands embedded in dense desmoplastic stroma (H&E).
Cholangiocarcinoma (high power): marked nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia and loss of polarity in infiltrating biliary glands.

fields.label: Precursor lesion (BilIN / IPNB)
options: Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile ducts (IPNB)

reference.title: Biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN) & bile duct margin dysplasia
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition uses a two-tier grading system for flat biliary dysplasia: low-grade BilIN vs high-grade BilIN (carcinoma in situ). Distinguishing high-grade BilIN from reactive stent atypia is critical at frozen section and final bile duct margins.
reference.note: Photomicrograph from Wikimedia Commons under an open Creative Commons licence. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Low-grade vs High-grade BilIN
points: Low-grade BilIN: pseudostratified nuclei with mild-to-moderate atypia confined to the basal two-thirds and preserved polarity.
High-grade BilIN (CIS): full-thickness loss of polarity, marked pleomorphism, complex micropapillary/cribriform tufting, and aberrant p53 / loss of SMAD4.

images.caption: Low-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN): pseudostratified columnar epithelium with mild-to-moderate atypia and retained polarity.

reference.title: Extrahepatic bile duct resection margins
reference.intro: Evaluate proximal and distal bile duct mucosal margins separately for invasive carcinoma and high-grade BilIN (low-grade BilIN at a margin does not require re-resection), plus the radial periductal soft tissue and hepatic parenchymal margins.
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Bile duct & radial soft tissue margins
points: Proximal and distal bile duct margins: report invasive carcinoma and high-grade BilIN separately; note any intraoperative frozen-section revision.
Radial / periductal soft tissue margin: ink the entire periductal soft tissue and hepatic artery / portal vein groove; positive radial margin is the most common site of R1 resection.
